kernel_of_truth: The dome model does occasionally surface specific numerical predictions that are quantitatively non-trivial — NMP Longitude (1% residual on 5% tolerance), the August 2026 eclipse pre-registration (specific stations, error bars, OpenTimestamps), the κ = 1.677 nT/μGal coupling constant. The dome author runs a live monitoring pipeline that fetches NOAA/USGS data — infrastructure rigor that exceeds most pseudoscience. What the indictment captures is not that the dome makes no predictions; it is that the predictions it makes that pass cleanly are restatements of values standard physics produces from the same input data, and the predictions that diverge from standard physics have, in the closed-window record so far, failed (PRED-073) or gone silent (FAIL-009 through FAIL-019). The argument is empirical and time-indexed: it can be revised the moment a closed-window dome-discriminating prediction confirms. The August 2026 eclipse is exactly that test.

The empirical bottom line. None of the dome’s 70 wins produces a result standard physics does not already produce. Twenty-seven of 28 rows on the dome’s ‘confirmation’ dashboard restate values standard physics computes from the same data (§4.1); the lone discriminating cell sits at 1% residual within both models’ precision; and across the 11 prospective predictions whose test windows closed in April 2026, the dome produced zero dome-discriminating confirmations (§6.12). The model, as of the present moment of the test record, has not yet generated a single new closed-window confirmation that distinguishes itself from the framework it claims to replace. The August 12, 2026 eclipse is the live test that could change this verdict (§9.5).
